content.thinking: I will read the feature flag service, library, and toggle action.

The bugs are now clear.

Tracing the toggle-flag logic shows the override-off case should actually work. The early return only fires when the flag state matches the requested state, so disabling an enabled override correctly proceeds to deletion.

Re-examining the toggle-flag logic shows the early return is not the culprit. When turning an override off, isEnabled returns true while input.enabled is false, so the condition fails and execution proceeds to deletion. The bug must be elsewhere.

toggleFlag deletion looks correct. The bug may instead be in updateOrg merging settings without replacing the array. A second issue was found: non-overridable flags are incorrectly allowed to be overridden when their strategy is "plan".

isEnabled checks stored overrides before strategy, so a non-overridable flag can still be forced on by an admin. The fix should reject all non-overridable flags regardless of strategy.

Reconsidering the toggle-flag logic. The early return might be inverted in a subtle way, or the bug could stem from a Free plan scenario where kanban is initially disabled.

The organization-repository updateOrg function merges overrides by concatenating current and patch values instead of replacing them.

The concatenation logic preserves existing overrides when the patch is empty. Disabling one flag therefore leaves the rest intact instead of removing only that specific override.

Replacing the entire overrides array would require callers to always pass the full desired list. Partial patches omitting overrides would then wipe existing ones. The current concatenation preserves existing entries when the field is absent.

Overrides are a set to merge. Patching one flag never drops the others.

The merge logic prevents deletions from sticking. toggleFlag already sends the full desired set, so replacing the array directly would correctly remove only the target override while preserving the rest.

A safer approach replaces the overrides array only when the field is explicitly present in the patch. If the client omits it, the existing set remains untouched.

Spreading `patch.settings` directly would overwrite the existing overrides array with undefined if the client omits the field. The replacement logic must explicitly check whether the key is present before overwriting.

Object spread replacement is the right fix because toggleFlag already sends the complete desired set. I should check whether any tests expect union merge behavior before changing it. There is also a second bug to investigate.

The second bug is in toggleFlag. It should reject requests to enable non-overridable flags regardless of strategy. isEnabled must also ignore overrides for non-overridable flags. Currently toggleFlag runs before the action checks equality, so a user trying to enable a non-overridable feature on a free plan gets an error instead of the plan's true state being respected.

The action early return problem requires more careful attention.

The early return bug may stem from repository merge logic. When toggleFlag deletes the override flag, a subsequent union with current data restores it. The action then reports success while the override remains stored as on.

The repository merge is bug 1. The action early return is not a separate bug; the override keeps isEnabled true, so the action correctly skips toggling when the flag is already on.

Overrides only turn features on. They cannot force a feature off when the plan already enables it. Removing an override key should simply delete that override entry. The feature remains enabled by the underlying plan rule.

I will implement the two fixes.

isEnabled will only apply overrides when a flag is marked overridable. toggleFlag will reject non-overridable flags and throw an error. Existing Error messages remain for backward compatibility. If a non-overridable flag is already enabled, the action returns success without storing. If the user tries to enable it, toggleFlag throws.

Stored overrides for non-overridable flags remain in storage but have no effect. toggleFlag throws before writing when a user requests enabling a flag that is already disabled by plan, so the existing override persists.

The repository patch logic preserves existing overrides by default. It only replaces them when the patch explicitly provides an empty array, which clears all stored overrides.

toggleFlag passes the complete override list, so unrelated overrides remain intact. I will update a misleading comment and clarify that the service check is the real gate, not the action comment.

content.text: The override list is merged instead of replaced, so a switch-off never drops a flag, and plan-gated flags ignore the `overridable` flag. I'll fix both.
